metadata.topic: Energy — Advantages and Disadvantages of Wind Turbines
metadata.note: 4m: 2 advantages × 1m + 2 disadvantages × 1m. Caribbean context: question explicitly asks about wind turbines 'in some Caribbean countries'. Advantages: renewable / no greenhouse gases. Disadvantages: intermittent (wind-dependent) / high initial cost. Multiple correct tokens per slot — any 2 valid advantages and any 2 valid disadvantages earn full marks.

question.name: CSEC Phy Jun 2023 Q2b — Wind Turbine Advantages and Disadvantages (Caribbean)
question.text:
State TWO advantages and TWO disadvantages of using wind turbines in some Caribbean countries.

Advantages:

Advantage 1: [[1]]

Advantage 2: [[2]]

Disadvantages:

Disadvantage 1: [[3]]

Disadvantage 2: [[4]]
question.general_feedback:
Wind turbines in Caribbean countries:

Advantages:

  • Renewable energy source — wind is inexhaustible and naturally replenished
  • No greenhouse gas emissions — produces no CO₂ or other pollutants during operation
  • Caribbean trade winds — consistent easterly trade winds provide reliable generation potential
  • Low running costs — once installed, fuel costs are zero

Disadvantages:

  • Intermittent supply — output depends on wind speed; no generation when wind is calm or too strong
  • High initial/installation cost — turbines and grid connection are expensive to install
  • Visual and noise pollution — large turbines affect landscape and produce low-frequency noise
  • Hazard to wildlife — rotating blades can harm birds and bats

groups.label: Advantage 1 of wind turbines (Caribbean context)
groups.diagnostic_hint: Wind is a RENEWABLE energy source — it will not run out. In the Caribbean, consistent trade winds make it particularly viable, unlike coal or oil which must be imported.

options.text: No greenhouse gas emissions during operation
Intermittent output dependent on wind speed

groups.label: Advantage 2 of wind turbines (Caribbean context)
groups.diagnostic_hint: Wind turbines produce NO greenhouse gas emissions during operation (no combustion). This reduces carbon footprint compared to burning fossil fuels.

options.text: Intermittent output dependent on wind speed
No greenhouse gas emissions during operation

groups.label: Disadvantage 1 of wind turbines (Caribbean context)
groups.diagnostic_hint: Wind energy is INTERMITTENT — when wind speed is too low or too high, turbines cannot generate electricity reliably. This is a key limitation in areas with variable wind.

options.text: Intermittent output dependent on wind speed
No greenhouse gas emissions during operation

groups.label: Disadvantage 2 of wind turbines (Caribbean context)
groups.diagnostic_hint: Wind turbines have HIGH initial installation costs. However, running costs are low since no fuel is needed. The payback period can be many years.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 7 tokens: 3 advantages (correct for slots 1–2), 3 disadvantages (correct for slots 3–4), 1 trap token. Advantage slots (1 & 2): any 2 of {Renewable, No greenhouse gases, Low running costs} earn marks. 'Reliable 24/7 supply' is the trap — wind is NOT reliable around the clock (it is intermittent), so this is factually wrong as an advantage. Disadvantage slots (3 & 4): any 2 of {Intermittent, High cost, Visual/noise pollution} earn marks. 'Reliable 24/7 supply' is implicitly a disadvantage in disguise but is presented as a token — the negative framing in the word bank prevents confusion. Caribbean-specific note: the question context (Caribbean countries) makes 'trade winds' relevant but the core answers are the same anywhere.
